scope: Independent regional and language framing review of eight current drafts, using retained primary source checks; no new identity assertions.
checks: Bhukha is explicitly Sambalpuri-language and western Odisha context is named; no dialect classification or cultural hierarchy imposed.
Flagship distinguishes state cinema from one cultural centre, and cross-language actor section explicitly identifies Ankur as Hindi.
Sadhu profile separates Odia filmmaking from Odisha-connected work in Hindi.
Nandita birthplaceBombay, upbringingDelhi and family/childhoodBaripada connections remain distinct; no Odisha birthplace claim.
Zwigato language claim is based on official Hindi/Odia field, separately from Bhubaneswar setting. Manto selection not claimed as Odia-language film.
DAMaN original Odia and later Hindi-dubbed release distinguished; film Malkangiri setting not projected onto worker-study districts.
Maya Miriga, Parbati and Manmohan discussions do not infer film language or personal identity from surname/location alone.
No universal claim that a regional film represents all residents or all cinema in a language.
